children: STOCKHOLM--Swedish state-owned energy company Vattenfall said  it would build a large battery-storage facility at its Brunsbuttel site in Germany.

The project, to be built on the site of the Brunsbuttel nuclear power plant which is currently being decommissioned, will have a storage capacity of around 1,000 megawatt hours, making it one of Germany's largest battery storage projects, the company said Thursday.
The battery and its connection to the grid are expected to be operational by the end of 2028.
"Batteries play a key role in the future energy system, balancing electricity demand and supply," said Claus Wattendrup, head of solar and batteries at Vattenfall.
"As generation from solar and wind power continues to grow, powerful storage solutions are essential for strengthening energy security and reducing dependence on fossil fuel imports."
